function: Joint transmit beamforming and power allocation at an ISAC roadside unit, learned by a spiking-network actor-critic DRL policy to maximize sum-rate under CRLB sensing constraints (p. 6-7, 9).
system: Mono-static ISAC RSU with 32 transmit and 32 receive antennas (ULA), three single-antenna vehicles on a road, 30 GHz carrier; no RIS (p. 3, 10).
method: Model-free actor-critic DRL with policy clipping whose actor and critic are spiking neural networks (LIF neurons, surrogate gradient), trained online by interaction (p. 8-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: ULA steering vectors, power-law path loss, radar echo and vehicle-motion models, no channel dataset; K = 3 vehicles, N = 100 time slots (p. 4-5, 10).
test_conditions: Trained and evaluated in the same three-vehicle scenario with fixed initial positions and random speeds; evaluation sweeps maximum transmit power 0-40 dBm and time steps (p. 10-12).
baselines: Non-learned: random scheme; learned: PPO, DDPG, DQN (p. 11).
metrics: Cumulative reward, training and inference energy consumption, achievable sum-rate versus time and maximum power, RMSE of angle and distance estimation (p. 11-13).
complexity: FLOPs formulas of the spiking and baseline networks mapped to energy: 5.15x less energy in training and 7.125x in inference than PPO/DDPG (p. 3, 11, 12).
openness: none (no code or data link or availability statement in the paper).
q1_support: p. 5: "denote the path loss at reference distance d0" defines a custom path-loss model; p. 10: "We consider a scenario with three vehicles" sets up its own simulator. No 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 12: "we vary the maximum transmit power at the RSU" is a power sweep in the same scenario as training (three vehicles, 32 antennas, p. 10); no other scenario, vehicle count or antenna number is tested.
q3_support: p. 11: "Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) [26], Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) [44], DQN [30], and Random scheme"; p. 12: "highest sum-rate across all transmit power levels, outperforming baseline algorithms such as PPO, DDPG, DQN, and Random allocation"
q4_support: p. 11: "the total number of floating-point operations (FLOPs) is used to quantify the computational workload during training and inference"; p. 3: "achieves energy savings of 5.15 times during model training and 7.125 times during inference compared to conventional approaches"
q5_support: p. 10: "We consider a scenario with three vehicles (i.e., K = 3)" is a self-built simulation; the paper gives no code or data link and no availability statement.
notes: ISAC V2X: the learned policy chooses the beamforming matrix and power of the RSU (p. 7), a physical-layer decision, so area 5. q3 rests on DDPG, DQN and the random scheme; the PPO baseline uses the same policy-clipping algorithm as the proposed method with ordinary networks (p. 12), so it is close to an ablation. q4: the cost is given as FLOPs-based energy (Fig. 4b-c, p. 11), with no absolute FLOP counts, parameter counts or runtime; reviewer to confirm.
